newsitem.title: USA: Illinois governor plans push for education funding.
newsitem.headline: Illinois governor plans push for education funding.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar will continue to push for education funding reform in the legislature in the wake of the state supreme court's dismissal on Friday of a constitutional challenge to the current funding system, the governor's spokesman said Friday.

Mike Lawrence said the court agreed with the governor's position that school funding was a legislative matter and not a judicial matter. Edgar was a defendant in the case filed in 1990 by a group of 75 school districts.

Lawrence said Edgar was finalizing a plan for a fairer school funding system that would not rely as much on local property taxes and that would also address spending inequities among school districts. He added the governor would likely come out with the plan during the spring session of the General Assembly.

Earlier this year, the governor supported a proposed constitutional amendment that would have required the state to fund at least 50 percent of education costs in exchange for lower local property taxes.
That proposal, however, failed to gain support in the General Assembly.
School district officials who filed the school funding lawsuit said its dismissal by the state's high court now shifts their focus to the legislature.
The dismissal followed previous rejections of the lawsuit by the Illinois Appellate Court in 1994 and by the Cook County Circuit Court in 1992.
